questions.question: Give the IUPAC name of the compound CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH(CH₂CH₃)CH₂OH.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Choose the parent chain.** The longest continuous chain containing the –OH group has six carbon atoms, so the parent is **hexane**. The –OH carbon must be numbered as C1.

$$\text{C1 (CH}_2\text{OH)} - \text{C2 [CH(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)]} - \text{C3 (CH}_2\text{) - C4 (CH}_2\text{) - C5 [CH(CH}_3\text{)] - C6 (CH}_3\text{)}$$

**Step 2 — Number the chain.** Numbering from the –OH end gives the hydroxy group locant 1; numbering from the other end would give it locant 6, which is not permitted.

**Step 3 — Identify substituents.** An ethyl group on C2 and a methyl group on C5.

**Step 4 — Assemble the name,** listing substituents alphabetically (ethyl before methyl) and adding the position and form of the suffix:

$$\boxed{\text{2-ethyl-5-methylhexan-1-ol}}$$

A hyphen is placed before a single-letter or single-digit prefix, and the final 'e' of the '-ane' is dropped before the vowel of '-ol'.
questions.knowledgeNote: The longest chain containing the –OH group is the parent, and numbering must give the hydroxy group the lowest locant.
